changelog: Rewrote [When to Segment] rule 4 to forbid boundaries inside incomplete coordinate structures (X and Y, X or Y) until ALL coordinates have arrived and the structure closes. Added explicit rule: 'Do not mark before the final coordinate arrives.'

Rewrote [When to Segment] rule 10 to forbid boundaries before negations, reversals, exclusive markers ('only', 'not', 'without', 'partially'), or scope-limiting modifiers that would overturn or restrict the preceding claim.

Added new [When to Segment] rule 11: 'After a prepositional phrase object arrives, if the phrase completes a noun phrase that is the object of a transitive verb.' This permits boundaries after the full NP closes, not before.

Expanded [Never Segment] rule 6 to explicitly forbid boundaries: (a) inside coordinate structures before the final coordinate; (b) after a noun heading a prepositional phrase, before the preposition's object; (c) before negations, exclusive markers, or scope-limiting modifiers that reverse or restrict the preceding assertion.

Rewrote [Priority Rules] to demote boundaries at relative position 0/3 (early in sentence) and after commas that precede incomplete coordinate structures or polarity reversals to lowest confidence. Ranked boundaries after COMPLETE coordinate structures and after polarity-settled clauses (negation/reversal fully visible) as highest confidence.

Clarified in [Priority Rules] that 'polarity settled' means the negation, reversal, or exclusive marker has already arrived and is visible in the emitted text, so the reader cannot be misled by what follows.
